claim: The owner edit form binds nested pet and visit fields: the owner binder disallows only id and *.id; the owner is loaded as a model attribute from the path id; Owner.pets is exposed through getPets() with cascade ALL and no @Valid, and Pet.visits (a Set with cascade ALL) is reachable by index; PetValidator is registered only on the pet binder; save() merges the detached owner (open-in-view is false), so pets[0].name, pets[0].birthDate or pets[0].visits[0].description are applied and persisted.
limitation: Binder, cascade and merge behaviour read from source and Spring data-binding rules; not run (no JDK on the audit machine, so the application tests were not run either). Visits are reachable only by index of an existing visit; a higher pets[n] index may also auto-grow the list and add new pets (Inferred). JPA-level bean validation may still reject blank names or over-long values at flush (Inferred). The same nested binding is reachable through the pet and visit routes, not only the owner edit form (see 15/R-13). Medium per the rubric: needs a reachable route (V-1) and bypasses PetValidator only.
